issues.legal_issue: A challenge to the quantum of compensation has no merit where a special leave petition against the impugned judgment has already been dismissed.
material_facts: The appeal challenged the quantum of compensation.
A special leave petition against the impugned judgment had been dismissed.
issues.conclusion: The appeal had no merit insofar as it challenged the quantum of compensation.
issues.legal_principle: The Court relied on the dismissal of the special leave petition against the impugned judgment; it cited no statutory provision or earlier case for this conclusion.

predicates.appeal_challenges_compensation_quantum: The appellant challenged the amount of compensation in an appeal.
predicates.prior_leave_challenge_dismissed: A prior special leave challenge to the impugned judgment was dismissed.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges compensation quantum and a prior special leave challenge to the same judgment has been dismissed, the quantum challenge fails.

issues.legal_issue: A claimant whose land compensation falls within the amended compensation scheme is entitled to the enhanced solatium provided by that scheme.
material_facts: The appeal concerned compensation for acquired land.

The Court held that the respondents were entitled to the benefit of Act 68 of 1984, which provided 30% solatium for the period described by the Court as running from publication to notification under Section 4(1).
issues.conclusion: The respondents were entitled to the amended solatium benefit.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied Act 68 of 1984 and referred to Section 4(1) in describing the period for which solatium was payable. It relied on no earlier case.

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning compensation for acquired land.
predicates.amended_solatium_scheme_applies: The compensation falls within an amended scheme that provides enhanced solatium.

issues.definition: In an appeal concerning compensation for acquired land, if the amended solatium scheme applies, the claimant receives enhanced solatium.

issues.legal_issue: A claimant is entitled to the amended rate of interest when the decision is given more than one year after the relevant point, with interest already received counted toward that entitlement.
material_facts: The appeal concerned compensation for acquired land.
The Court stated that its decision came after one year.
The respondents had already received interest at the lower rate.
The Court held that the respondents were entitled under Act 68 of 1984 to interest at the amended rate, with the interest already received counted toward it.
issues.conclusion: The respondents were entitled to interest at the amended rate, with the lower-rate interest already received credited toward that entitlement.
issues.legal_principle: Applying Act 68 of 1984, the Court held that where the decision was given after one year the respondents were entitled to interest at 9%, out of which they had already received 6%. It relied on no earlier case.

rule.if: land_acquisition_compensation_appeal and amended_interest_scheme_applies and decision_made_after_one_year and claimant_received_lower_interest

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning compensation for acquired land.
predicates.amended_interest_scheme_applies: The compensation falls within an amended scheme that provides a higher rate of interest.
predicates.decision_made_after_one_year: The decision was given more than one year after the relevant point.
predicates.claimant_received_lower_interest: The claimant had already received interest at a lower rate.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns land compensation, the amended interest scheme applies, the decision comes after one year, and the claimant has received lower-rate interest, the claimant receives enhanced interest with the prior interest credited.
